subsystems.name: Optical display
subsystems.role: overlays digital images on the real world without blocking the view.
parts: microdisplay (microLED, laser beam scanning or OLED)

subsystems.name: Sensing
subsystems.role: captures the scene and the wearer's context for visual analysis and input.

subsystems.name: Audio
subsystems.role: delivers private sound and picks up voice commands without earbuds.

subsystems.name: Compute and connectivity
subsystems.role: runs the AI agent, translation and vision models on the glasses or a paired phone.

subsystems.name: Power
subsystems.role: keeps the glasses light enough to wear all day while running the display and AI.

subsystems.name: Frame and thermal
subsystems.role: holds everything in a comfortable, stable shape and disperses heat.

buildSteps.title: Design the optical stack
buildSteps.detail: Simulate how light from a microdisplay travels through a waveguide and exits toward the eye, choosing a field of view and eye box that balance size, weight and image quality.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the waveguide
buildSteps.detail: Pattern nanoscale gratings onto a glass or polymer wafer using nanoimprint or etching, then dice and polish it into a thin combiner.

buildSteps.title: Build the microdisplay
buildSteps.detail: Make a tiny high-brightness panel — for example a microLED array or a laser beam scanner — that can be focused into the waveguide.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the optical engine
buildSteps.detail: Align the microdisplay, collimating lenses and waveguide under a microscope, then fix them in place with UV-cured adhesive.

buildSteps.title: Integrate electronics
buildSteps.detail: Place the system-on-chip, sensors, battery and bone-conduction transducers into the frame, routing flexible circuits through the temples.

buildSteps.title: Develop the AI software
buildSteps.detail: Train and compress models for speech recognition, translation, scene understanding and a conversational agent, then optimise them to run on a phone or the glasses' own chip.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate and align
buildSteps.detail: Adjust the display so virtual images sit correctly for the wearer's eyes, and calibrate the camera and IMU so the AI knows what the wearer is looking at.

buildSteps.title: Test and validate
buildSteps.detail: Check optical clarity, battery life, heat, drop and sweat resistance, and run user trials for translation accuracy and comfort over a full day.

prerequisites.why: they are the only practical way to put a transparent, high-contrast image in front of the eye without a bulky prism.
running large language and vision models on a device that weighs under 100 g without draining the battery is still a challenge.
it provides private sound and leaves the ear canal open, which is important for safety and situational awareness.
cloud services translate many languages well, but on-device, low-latency translation in noisy places is not yet reliable.
the glasses need enough energy for a day of display, sensing and AI in a package that fits behind the ear.

pathway.milestone: audio-only smart glasses with a camera and voice assistant
pathway.unlocks: hands-free photos, calls, and basic AI queries in a familiar glasses form.

pathway.milestone: monocular waveguide display showing notifications and live translation
pathway.unlocks: useful heads-up information for travellers, technicians and people with hearing loss.

pathway.milestone: on-device large language and vision models running for hours
pathway.unlocks: private, low-latency visual analysis and conversation without a constant cloud connection.

pathway.milestone: wide field-of-view, all-day battery and natural social acceptability
pathway.unlocks: everyday augmented reality where digital and physical worlds blend seamlessly.
